The units are completely off here. Pounds in the english system are already a unit of force, so pound-feet is a unit of work. This differs from the SI system, where the common unit is kilograms, which is a unit of MASS, not FORCE. Also, you cannot find the "force" of a raindrop by dividing its mass by it's terminal velocity. grams/centimeter, or ounces/inch make NO sense as units.

A Newton (N) is the general unit used to measure force. It is defined as a (Kilogram * Meter)/(Second^2) In other words, mass times distance divided by time twice. Thus your unit of grams/centimeter is mass divided by distance, and ounces/inch is force divided by distance, and neither work for comparison
